name: cldr
description: Money formatted as currency in the locales the documentation and tests use: every display (symbol, narrow symbol, code, name) and sign (standard, accounting), digits and rounding, amounts beyond a double's digits, the Intl options ducat passes on (signDisplay, useGrouping, minimumIntegerDigits, fraction and significant digits, roundingIncrement, roundingMode, roundingPriority, trailingZeroDisplay), and the options format and Intl refuse; the text and its parts.

provenance.method: Unicode TR35's number and currency formatting (https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-numbers.html), with the Intl.NumberFormat options ducat passes on read as ECMA-402 defines them (SetNumberFormatDigitOptions, FormatNumericToString, ToRawFixed, ToRawPrecision and GetNumberFormatPattern: https://tc39.es/ecma402/#sec-setnfdigitoptions; rounding on exact fractions, never a double; useGrouping's min2 and auto from CLDR's minimumGroupingDigits), and the parse rules of docs/reference/parse.md, implemented with Python's standard library over the CLDR 48.0 JSON snapshot in data/cldr/ (data/cldr/README.md), independently of ducat's TypeScript and of ICU. ducat formats and parses through the runtime's Intl, whose ICU 78.3 carries CLDR 48, so passing these vectors means two independent implementations agree on the same CLDR release. TR35 doesn't define formatToParts: here the number's digits, separators and signs are the integer, group, decimal, fraction and minusSign parts, the symbol or name is the currency part, bidi marks (format characters) in a symbol are literals, and every other pattern character, including currency spacing, is a literal; adjacent characters of one type merge. That convention, and how a currency name is shown (the number in the decimal pattern with the currency's separators, never in the accounting form, then unitPattern with the name in the number's plural form), were settled after looking at ICU's output, so agreement on them is not independent evidence; the text of every other row is. So was the explicit plus sign (signDisplay always and exceptZero) where TR35 leaves it open: the negative subpattern with its minus sign replaced by the plus sign, or, where the negative subpattern has no minus sign (accounting's parentheses) or there is none, the plus sign before the positive subpattern. So were the notation rules where ECMA-402 leaves the data to the implementation (spec/README.md): which compact pattern applies (CLDR's short currency patterns for a symbol or code, the decimal ones of compactDisplay for a name; by the rounded magnitude and the mantissa's plural form, CLDR's explicit 1 form for a positive mantissa only; its negative subpattern or the minus sign before it), the compact part without the default ignorables around it, min2 grouping by default in compact notation, the plural form of a name (the amount's in compact notation, the whole value's with its exponent in scientific, the first holding category by name), and V8's locale matching (best fit is lookup). fr-CH is left out: CLDR 48's common/main/fr_CH.xml (unicode-org/cldr, tag release-48, lines 215-217) sets only currencyDecimal "." for latn, so its group separator is inherited from fr, U+202F, while ICU 78.3's icu4c/source/data/locales/fr_CH.txt (unicode-org/icu, tag release-78.3, lines 10-13, sha256 ffb73f672e4bb219dbbdeacf25d98bfafc1f30f85003dc90725556f5cc7b2ef8, copied to data/icu/fr_CH.txt) sets symbols{ currencyDecimal{"."} group{"'"} }. fr-CH's rows are in the icu-overrides files instead.

data.runtimeIntl: every row: ducat formats and parses with the runtime's Intl (ICU 78.3, CLDR 48 on Node 24 and Bun); an engine with other CLDR data writes other text
